source.stem: Why is the circulatory system of mammals described as a double circulation?

options.text: Blood flows firstly through arteries and then through veins.
Blood flows through the heart twice on one complete circuit of the body.
In the heart, blood flows firstly through atria and then through ventricles.
The atria and the ventricles contract alternately.

intelligence.enrichment: Cells have three main parts: the cell membrane, cytoplasm, and nucleus. The cell membrane encloses the cytoplasm and nucleus, separates cells, and allows useful materials in and wastes out; the cytoplasm contains cell components and many life processes occur there; the nucleus regulates cell activities and growth. Cell part identity -> specific role in boundary control, life processes, or regulation. The learner correctly applies this rule: Cells have three main parts: the cell membrane, cytoplasm, and nucleus. The cell membrane encloses the cytoplasm and nucleus, separates cells, and allows useful materials in and wastes out; the cytoplasm contains cell components and many life processes occur there; the nucleus regulates cell activities and growth. The nucleus is the important part, so it does every major job inside the cell.
